newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Kabila still in Angola, not at Zaire talks.
newsitem.headline: Kabila still in Angola, not at Zaire talks.

text.p: Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila was still in Angola on Saturday afternoon awaiting the return of South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki, who was to have escorted him to a peace summit, South African and Angolan officials said.
An earlier report that Kabila had left was premature, the officials said.

A senior Western diplomat had told Reuters he believed Kabila had left Luanda to meet Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko for internationally-sponsored peace talks on a South African navy vessel off the coast of West Africa.
The Ugandan jet which brought Kabila to the Angolan capital left the city at 9.40 a.m. (0840 GMT) on Saturday, apparently leading to the confusion.
Angolan presidential spokesman Aldemiro vaz de Concicao told Reuters the Zairean rebel alliance leader was still at the Futungo presidential compound outside Luanda where he had spent Friday night.
"Mr Kabila is waiting for Mr Mbeki to come back to Luanda. He is still where you saw him last night," the spokesman said.

South African officials also said reports of Kabila's departure were inaccurate. Declining to elaborate why Kabila was still in Luanda, one official added: "We have no details on whether Mr Mbeki will come to Luanda to escort Mr Kabila to the ship."
Kabila had arrived in the Angolan capital on Friday from the rebel stronghold of Lubumbashi in southeast Zaire to travel with Mbeki to the talks in international waters.
But the rebel leader pulled out of the arrangements late on Friday, demanding guarantees of his security on the converted icebreaker and a say in the composition of the summit.

Mbeki left the Angolan capital to discuss Kabila's concerns with talks chairman President Nelson Mandela of South Africa on Friday evening and had been due to return to Luanda on Saturday to brief Kabila about security measures.
South African officials said on Saturday morning Mbeki was still on the ship.
